To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the in vitro binding properties of [3H]-nimodipine (L-type calcium channel antagonist) and [3H]-CGS-1975S (NMDA receptor antagonist) were unchanged in ischemic brain compared to nonischemic brain, despite the fact that the in vivo binding properties of both of these compounds were increased in ischemia.
ischemia-induced changes of calcium channel function in vivo are not reflected in changes of calcium channel binding in vitro.
the ischemic-induced changes of calcium channel function, previously identified with in vivo binding studies, were not observed in vitro with [3H] nimodipine and CGS-19755.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new calcium channel ligands and the use of these compounds in the study of calcium channel function in focal cerebral ischemia.
the effect of focal ischemia on the binding of calcium channel ligands to rat brain.
the effect of focal brain ischemia on calcium channel function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ischemia-induced alterations in calcium channel function cannot be detected by in vitro binding of [H]nimodopine and [3]CGS- 19755 to ischemia rat brain.
in vitro binding of both calcium channel ligands is not altered by 4 h of cerebral ischemia.
the in vivo binding methods used to measure calcium channel function are not applicable in ischemic brain tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the in vitro method of quantification of [3H]-nimodipine binding is more sensitive in detecting ischemia-related changes in calcium channel activity than is in vivo autoradiography, whereas in vitro binding of [H]CGS 19755 to ischemia is not sensitive enough to detect ischemia-related changes.
the in vivo binding methods are more sensitive to ischemia-induced alterations in calcium channel function.

in vitro binding of [ 3H ]nimodipine to rat brain failed to identify changes in L-type VSCCs in the ischemic brain and in vitro binding of CGS-19755 failed to identify changes of NMDA receptor-linked calcium channels in the ischemic rat brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in vitro binding of [H3]nimodipne and [H3]CGS- 19755 to rat cortex and striatum following focal cerebral ischemia does not detect ischemia-induced changes in calcium channels previously reported by in vitro binding methods.
in vitro binding methods are not sensitive enough to identify ischemic changes in the in vivo binding of [3h]nimodipin or [3H] CGS-19755.
in vitro autoradiography of brain tissue is an unreliable method to study calcium channel function in focal cerebral ischemia.
